subject.title: [Bug]: Concurrent allow-always approvals silently lose allowlist entries (last-write-wins race in exec-approvals.json)

question: Should the stale exec approval write fix land through the broader CAS/locking direction in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78226, through a narrower replacement for this allow-always race, or through the broader runtime-state separation design?
rationale: All viable fixes change persistence semantics for exec approval security state and can interact with admin revocations, so a maintainer should choose the durable contract before automation opens another repair branch.

options.title: Adopt guarded core write path
options.body: Rework or replace the open CAS/locking PR so every allow-always and usage write reloads, merges, or verifies current approval state before saving.

options.title: Narrow this issue only
options.body: Land a focused allow-always merge-under-lock fix while leaving broader metadata/admin-revocation races to the linked security issue.

options.title: Defer to state separation
options.body: Pause code changes until maintainers decide whether mutable runtime metadata should move out of `exec-approvals.json`.

recommendation.title: Adopt guarded core write path
recommendation.body: Rework or replace the open CAS/locking PR so every allow-always and usage write reloads, merges, or verifies current approval state before saving.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent approval-store and default-write commits make this the strongest available routing candidate for the persistence contract choice.
